newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania asks Italy to re-equip army, police.
newsitem.headline: Albania asks Italy to re-equip army, police.

text.p: Albania asked Italy on Thursday to help re-equip its security forces and Rome said it was heading towards agreement with Tirana for the Italian navy to patrol Albanian waters to deter a chaotic exodus.
Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta, speaking after talks with Albanian Foreign Minister Arjan Starova, also said Italy had no plans for imminent military intervention in Albania.
"The foreign minister asked for the cooperation of the Italian government to re-equip military and police forces," Andreatta said.
A large part of Albania's security forces melted away in the upheavals of the past few weeks. Many soldiers and police deserted as crowds looted armouries of their weapons.
More than 10,000 Albanian refugees have arrived in Italy since March 13 aboard rusty, ancient ships.

"We examined the situation of the anarchy that exists (in the waters between Italy and Albania) and we began the process of re-activating agreements between our navy and Albania regarding control, including in Albanian territorial waters, through patrolling the (Albanian) coast," he said.

Some 130 Albanian ships, many of them military, arrived in Italy after local port authorities lost control. Italian coast guards say this represents between 60 and 70 percent of Albania's military and merchant fleets.
Andreatta said Starova told him the government was slowly regaining control.
Both agreed that economic, humanitarian and military aid to the Balkan country should take place in the framework of the European Union.
"Italian intervention, much less unilateral Italian intervention, is not at all foreseeable today, in the coming hours," Andreatta said.
EU foreign ministers are due to meet on Monday to discuss how they can help Albania.
"We are very optimistic and we expect that a good decision will be made (by the EU)," Starova told reporters.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, has been rocked by unrest since the collapse in January of shady "get-rich-quick" savings schemes. The protests mushroomed this month into armed rebellion in the south and chaos has spread across the country.

The two ministers met as the Italian navy completed a dramatic rescue of an overcrowded Albanian refugee ship, the Rozafa I, which had risked sinking in high seas off the Albanian coast with 350 people on board.

The frigate Espero towed the fishing boat to a bay north of the Albanian port of Durres. The refugees, 45 of them children, were given food and water and then taken by landing craft to a beach in the Bay of Rodon.

Coastguard officials in Brindisi said no boats carrying refugees had been seen heading for southern Italian shores on Thursday morning. They said strong winds and choppy seas would probably deter crossings during the day.

Italian authorities continued the repatriation of Albanian "undesirables", including some believed to have escaped from prisons during the upheaval and refugees who have broken the law since they arrived in Italy.
Around 100 were due to be sent home on Thursday, joining nearly 300 repatriated on Wednesday.
